subject.title: fix(agents): stop runs at the critical tool-loop threshold

question: Should loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay:false intentionally disable both Codex-native loop-detection relays, including PostToolUse outcome recording, rather than only the PreToolUse marker?
rationale: This is an existing user-facing configuration contract whose broadened opt-out affects whether native Codex tool outcomes can participate in critical-loop protection; the patch documents the choice but cannot establish product compatibility intent by itself.

options.title: Confirm the paired opt-out
options.body: Keep the documented behavior that false disables both loop-detection-only native relays while required policy and middleware relays remain installed.

options.title: Preserve PostToolUse detection
options.body: Keep the native outcome relay active when false disables only the PreToolUse subprocess, then update implementation and focused tests to preserve that narrower existing setting meaning.

recommendation.title: Confirm the paired opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the documented behavior that false disables both loop-detection-only native relays while required policy and middleware relays remain installed.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the implementation rationale and proof, but a current agents/Codex runtime owner should make the final contract decision.
